implementation_notes: Jackson is the dominant runtime realization: annotate the DTO with @JsonFilter("fields") and register a SimpleBeanPropertyFilter for that id in a filter provider built per request - filterOutAllExcept(set) serializes only the named properties. The filter lives in the serialization pipeline, so the projection costs no extra DTO and works for nested types that carry the same filter id. Validate the names against the DTO first: the filter itself silently ignores what it does not know.
pitfalls: filterOutAllExcept silently drops unknown property names, so a typo yields a smaller payload instead of an error - validate against the DTO/Jackson introspection first.
A FilterProvider is cheap to build but not thread-safe to mutate; build it per request and never cache it in a shared ObjectMapper field.
Filters only apply where the filter id matches: nested types need @JsonFilter too, and mixing @JsonFilter with @JsonView or @JsonIncludeProperties makes the effective shape hard to reason about.
The filter runs during serialization, so the resource is fully materialized (and every getter may already have been called) before the projection discards fields.

variants.name: Spring Data projection interfaces / DTO projections
variants.idiom_name: interface-based or record DTO projections, optionally selected dynamically per request
variants.implementation_notes: On the persistence side the view is a type: a closed projection interface (only accessors that match entity properties) or a record DTO makes Spring Data limit the selected columns, and a dynamic projection parameter (<T> query(..., Class<T> type)) chooses the view at invocation time. A runtime fields parameter then maps onto a bounded catalog of projection types - which is exactly the point: the vocabulary is compiled, so nothing arbitrary reaches the query.
pitfalls: Open projections (@Value SpEL expressions) disable the column-limiting optimisation, because the expression may touch any property.
Nested/recursive projections fetch the whole associated entity and then wrap it, so the saving stops at the top level.
Dynamic projections cannot validate a caller-supplied field list - keep the set of projection types closed, or the class parameter becomes an injection point.
